transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name], and I'll be talking with you today. Can you tell me what's been going on that brought you in?

Well… I guess what brought me in is that I’m having a really hard time keeping my mind on one thing. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but at work, if a saw starts up, or someone walks past the office, or even if I just think of another job I need to do, I’m pulled off whatever I was doing. Then I try to get back to it, but the whole day can kind of get away from me. I’m not sure if that’s the sort of thing you mean.
Do you find it hard to stay focused on tasks or activities in other situations, like at home or when you're trying to relax, or is this mainly a problem at work?

It’s… mostly noticeable at work, I think, because that’s where there’s always something happening. Like I said, one saw starts up or someone walks by, or I remember some other job, and I’m off track before I even realize it. Then I look up and somehow the whole day’s gotten away from me.

At home or trying to relax, I guess it can happen too, but work is where it causes the most trouble. I don’t know if that answers it right.
When you're at home or during times when you're trying to relax, do you also find it hard to stay focused on what you're doing, or does your mind tend to wander easily?

Yes… I mean, it can. I notice it most at work because it causes problems there, but even at home if I’m trying to sit with something, my mind can wander off pretty easily. It’s like one little noise or just a thought about something else I should do, and I’m not really with what I was doing anymore.

I don’t mean to make it sound dramatic, but it does feel like I can’t keep my mind on one thing the way I used to. Does that make sense?
Can you think of times when this difficulty staying focused happens outside of work and home, like when you're with friends, in meetings, or in other social situations?

I think so, yes. I mean, I notice it most at work because that’s where it really shows, but it can happen other places too. If I’m with people and something moves nearby or there’s noise, or even if I suddenly think of something else I’m supposed to do, I can kind of lose the thread of what’s happening.

It’s not that I don’t care or I’m trying to be rude. My mind just gets pulled off, and then I’m trying to come back and figure out where I was. I don’t know if that’s what you mean, but that’s how it feels.
Do you often feel restless, fidgety, or as though you can't sit still for very long, especially in situations where others might expect you to remain calm or focused?

A little, yes. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but if I have to sit at the desk doing estimates, or sit through a long meeting, I start feeling kind of wound up inside. Like I should be able to just stay put and finish, but my body wants to get up and move around.

Even with my wrist healed, it’s not really about pain or anything. It’s more just… sitting there feels harder than it should. I try to keep myself calm and not be distracting, but inside I feel pretty restless. Does that answer what you mean?
